fiches.source: Programme des enseignements de specialite des classes de premiere et terminale de la serie STI2D (arrete du 17 janvier 2019, NOR MENE1901591A, Bulletin officiel special n 1 du 22 janvier 2019) : developpement durable, architecture et construction (AC), systemes d'information et numerique (SIN), methodologie de projet et langues vivantes techniques. Tronc commun : arrete du 17 janvier 2019 (NOR MENE1901585A, langues vivantes) et programme d'enseignement moral et civique. Ressources : eduscol « Programmes et ressources en serie STI2D », « Developpement durable » et « Baccalaureat technologique STI2D » ; Agenda 2030 des Nations unies et objectifs de developpement durable.
points: La soutenance est un temps d'evaluation ou l'equipe presente son projet et repond aux questions du jury.
Elle comprend generalement un expose suivi d'un entretien avec les examinateurs.
L'expose suit un fil conducteur : contexte et besoin, demarche, realisations, essais, resultats et conclusion critique.
Un plan annonce clairement les parties et le temps consacre a chacune.
Les supports de presentation doivent etre lisibles, avec peu de texte et des visualisations explicites.
Chaque member de l'equipe doit intervenir : le jury evalue aussi la repartition de la parole.
Une demonstration du prototype est plus convaincante qu'une simple description, a condition d'etre preparee et sure.
Les resultats sont presentes avec des indicateurs, des mesures et des comparaisons avec le cahier des charges.
Les limites et les erreurs doivent etre assumees : le jury attend une analyse critique, pas un discours commercial.
Pendant l'entretien, il faut ecouter la question, reformuler si besoin et repondre de facon structuree.
Une question peut porter sur un choix technique, une hypothèse, un resultat d'essai ou la contribution de chaque eleve.
La capitalisation consiste a conserver les documents, les essais et les enseignements pour les projets futurs.

questions.q: Quel est un plan d'expose efficace ?
options: Contexte, demarche, realisations, essais, conclusion critique
questions.correction: Le fil conducteur permet au jury de suivre la logique du projet.

questions.q: Comment doit etre un support de presentation ?
options: Lisible avec peu de texte et des visualisations
Avec toutes les pages du rapport
questions.correction: Le support accompagne la parole sans la remplacer.

questions.q: Que doit faire un membre face a une question qu'il n'a pas comprise ?
questions.correction: La reformulation securise la comprehension et montre l'ecoute.

questions.q: Quelle attitude est attendue face aux limites du projet ?
questions.correction: Une analyse critique est evaluee positivement.

questions.q: Quel element rend une demonstration fiable ?
options: Une preparation et des conditions surees
questions.correction: Une demonstration doit etre repetee et presenter peu de risques de panne.

questions.q: Qu'est-ce que la capitalisation ?
options: Conserver savoirs et livrables pour le futur
questions.correction: La capitalisation rend le travail reutilisable par la suite.

questions.q: Quel element est evalue en plus du resultat technique ?
options: La repartition de la parole et l'analyse critique
questions.correction: Le jury evalue aussi la communication et la reflexivite de l'equipe.

questions.q: Preparer le plan d'une soutenance de 10 minutes pour un projet de prototype, en repartissant le temps entre les membres.
questions.reponse: Introduction (1 minute, porte-parole) : contexte, besoin et objectifs du projet. Premiere partie (2 minutes, responsable conception) : analyse fonctionnelle, cahier des charges et choix de solution avec la grille de decision. Deuxieme partie (3 minutes, responsable technique) : modelisation, fabrication du prototype et problemes rencontres, avec des images. Troisieme partie (2 minutes, responsable essais) : protocole, mesures, comparaison aux exigences et limites observees. Conclusion (2 minutes, porte-parole avec l'equipe) : bilan, apports de chacun, pistes d'amelioration et remerciements. L'ensemble est repete deux fois avec un chronometre. Un support unique circule, avec une diapo par partie et une diapo de synthese des resultats. Les reponses aux questions sont preparees a partir des points faibles identifies.
questions.correction: On attend un fil conducteur, des temps, une repartition de parole et une preparation aux questions.

questions.q: Expliquer pourquoi la presentazione des limites d'un prototype est un element positif de la soutenance.
questions.reponse: Un prototype est une realisation intermediaire : il ne peut pas satisfaire toutes les exigences des la premiere version. Le jury sait cela et attend que l'equipe soit capable d'en prendre conscience.Presenter les limites, c'est demontrer que l'on a mesure les ecarts entre le cahier des charges et le resultat, compris les causes des defauts et identifie les actions d'amelioration. C'est aussi une preuve d'honnetete intellectuelle et de maturite : un candidat qui cache un defaut sera obligé de le reconnaitre a la question suivante, ce qui deteriore la qualite de l'echange. La conclusion peut alors proposer une nouvelle iteration du prototype avec le changement prioritaire et le moyen de le valider. Cette posture est exactement celle de l'ingenieur en conception : prouver, mesurer, corriger.
questions.correction: On lie autocritique, mesure des ecarts, credibilite et demarche iterative.

fiches.titre: ANT1 · Describing a technical system in English
fiches.source: Programme des enseignements de specialite des classes de premiere et terminale de la serie STI2D (arrete du 17 janvier 2019, NOR MENE1901591A, Bulletin officiel special n 1 du 22 janvier 2019) : developpement durable, architecture et construction (AC), systemes d'information et numerique (SIN), methodologie de projet et langues vivantes techniques. Tronc commun : arrete du 17 janvier 2019 (NOR MENE1901585A, langues vivantes) et programme d'enseignement moral et civique. Ressources : eduscol « Programmes et ressources en serie STI2D », « Developpement durable » et « Baccalaureat technologique STI2D » ; Agenda 2030 des Nations unies et objectifs de developpement durable.
points: Technical English uses precise, simple sentences to describe how a system works.
The present simple describes permanent functions : the sensor measures the temperature.
The passive voice is frequent when the action matters more than the author : the signal is amplified by the controller.
A technical description follows a logical order : purpose, components, operation and limits.
The purpose answers the question 'What is it for ?' : the device regulates the temperature of a room.
Components are named with technical nouns : sensor, actuator, controller, power supply, housing.
Sequencing words such as first, then and finally describe the operation step by step.
Quantities are expressed with units : 12 volts, 5 amperes, 200 millimetres, 0,5 second.
The modal can describes ability or possibility : the battery can supply 2 amperes for one hour.
The modal must expresses a requirement : the housing must resist water and dust.
Comparatives are useful to justify a choice : aluminium is lighter than steel, but it is more expensive.
Avoid vague words such as 'thing' or 'good' : replace them by the exact name or a measurable property.

questions.q: Which tense describes a permanent technical function ?
questions.correction: The present simple states what a component does permanently.

questions.q: Why use the passive voice in a technical text ?
options: To focus on the action and the result
questions.correction: The passive emphasises what happens rather than who does it.

questions.q: Which phrase states the purpose of a device ?
questions.correction: The purpose describes the service rendered by the system.

questions.q: Which word is a technical noun ?
questions.correction: An actuator is a component that produces an action.

questions.q: Which modal expresses a requirement ?
questions.correction: Must expresses obligation or a technical requirement.

questions.q: How to compare two materials correctly ?
options: Aluminium is more light than steel
questions.correction: The comparative of light is lighter, followed by than.

questions.q: Why avoid the word 'thing' in a report ?
options: It is vague and should be replaced by an exact name
It is only used in speech
questions.correction: Technical writing requires precise terminology.

questions.q: Write a short description of a temperature control system using purpose, components, operation and limits.
questions.reponse: A possible description is: 'This system maintains the temperature of a room at a set value. It contains a temperature sensor, a controller, a heating element and a power supply. First, the sensor measures the room temperature and sends an analog signal to the controller. Then, the controller compares the measured value with the setpoint. If the measured temperature is lower than the setpoint, the controller switches on the heating element. Finally, the system stops heating when the setpoint is reached. The system can maintain the temperature within one degree, but it cannot heat a room larger than twenty square metres.' This description uses the present simple for functions, can for ability, and precise nouns and units.
questions.correction: On attend les quatre parties, le present simple, des noms techniques precises et des units.

questions.q: Rewrite these vague sentences in precise technical English: 'The thing works quickly. The material is good. The machine is big.'
questions.reponse: The sentences can be rewritten as: 'The actuator responds within 0,2 second. The material has a tensile strength of 400 MPa. The machine occupies 1,2 cubic metre.' Each vague adjective is replaced by a measurable property with its unit. 'Works quickly' becomes a response time, 'good' becomes a mechanical property, and 'big' becomes a volume or an envelope dimension. This transformation is essential in a technical report because a reader must be able to verify the statement and compare it with a requirement. A precise description also avoids disputes: 'good' can mean different things to different people, while '400 MPa' has a single meaning.
questions.correction: On remplace chaque mot vague par une propriete mesurable avec son unité.

affichage.texte: Technical English favours precision: present simple for functions, passive for processes, exact nouns and units.

affichage.eq: Present simple + passive voice + modal can / must

fiches.titre: ANT2 · Reading a datasheet and a technical manual
fiches.source: Programme des enseignements de specialite des classes de premiere et terminale de la serie STI2D (arrete du 17 janvier 2019, NOR MENE1901591A, Bulletin officiel special n 1 du 22 janvier 2019) : developpement durable, architecture et construction (AC), systemes d'information et numerique (SIN), methodologie de projet et langues vivantes techniques. Tronc commun : arrete du 17 janvier 2019 (NOR MENE1901585A, langues vivantes) et programme d'enseignement moral et civique. Ressources : eduscol « Programmes et ressources en serie STI2D », « Developpement durable » et « Baccalaureat technologique STI2D » ; Agenda 2030 des Nations unies et objectifs de developpement durable.
points: A datasheet gives the characteristics of a component in a standardised form.
Most datasheets begin with a general description, a list of features and a table of absolute maximum ratings.
Absolute maximum ratings must never be exceeded : doing so can destroy the component.
Recommended operating conditions define the normal range of use, which is narrower than the absolute maximum.
Electrical characteristics give typical and maximum values for parameters such as supply voltage, current and power.
A parameter is often given with conditions, for example 'output current = 100 mA at 25 °C'.
The letter 'typ' means typical, 'max' means maximum and 'min' means minimum.
Timing diagrams show the sequence and the duration of signals, with parameters such as rise time and delay.
Package drawings give the dimensions and the pinout, which is the numbering and function of each pin.
A technical manual describes installation, configuration, operation, maintenance and troubleshooting.
Warning symbols and the terms 'caution' and 'danger' signal risks for the user or the equipment.
A good reading method consists in identifying the need, locating the relevant table and checking the conditions and units.

questions.q: What do absolute maximum ratings mean ?
options: Limits that must never be exceeded
questions.correction: Exceeding an absolute maximum can permanently damage the component.

questions.q: What does 'typ' mean in a datasheet ?
questions.correction: Typ indicates a typical value observed under given conditions.

questions.q: Where can you find the function of each pin ?
options: In the pinout or package drawing
questions.correction: The pinout gives the numbering and function of the pins.

questions.q: What is a timing diagram used for ?
questions.correction: Timing diagrams describe rise time, delay and signal order.

questions.q: Which term signals a risk of serious injury ?
questions.correction: Danger indicates a hazard that can cause serious injury.

questions.q: Why check the conditions attached to a parameter ?
options: Because the value is only valid under those conditions
questions.correction: A value without its conditions cannot be compared or reused safely.

questions.q: What should you do first when reading a datasheet ?
questions.correction: A targeted reading is faster and less error-prone.

questions.q: A datasheet states 'supply voltage: 4,5 to 5,5 V typ 5 V; absolute maximum 7 V'. Explain how to use these values for a design.
questions.reponse: The recommended supply range is 4,5 to 5,5 volts, with a typical value of 5 volts. The circuit should be designed to operate inside this range, for example with a regulated 5 V supply and a tolerance that keeps the voltage between 4,75 and 5,25 V. The absolute maximum of 7 V is not an operating range : it is the limit beyond which the component may be destroyed. A transient above 7 V, even for a short time, is forbidden. The designer must also check the conditions attached to other parameters, such as temperature and load, and protect the input against overvoltage if the environment is noisy. This distinction between operating range and absolute maximum is a common source of error.
questions.correction: On distingue plage de fonctionnement et limite absolue, avec exemple de regulation.

questions.q: Describe the method for finding the cause of a malfunction using a technical manual.
questions.reponse: One starts by identifying the symptoms precisely : error message, abnormal noise, incorrect output. The troubleshooting section of the manual usually gives a table of symptoms and possible causes. One checks the simplest causes first : power supply, connectors, fuses and settings. Then one follows the diagnostic procedure, which may require measuring voltages or reading error codes. Each test result is compared with the expected value given in the manual. If several causes are possible, one eliminates them one at a time to avoid masking the real fault. The manual also indicates warnings to respect during intervention, such as disconnecting the power before opening the housing. Finally, the intervention and the measured values are recorded for future maintenance.
questions.correction: On suit symptomes, table de depannage, causes simples, mesures et tracabilite.

affichage.eq: Operating conditions ≠ absolute maximum ratings

fiches.source: Programme des enseignements de specialite des classes de premiere et terminale de la serie STI2D (arrete du 17 janvier 2019, NOR MENE1901591A, Bulletin officiel special n 1 du 22 janvier 2019) : developpement durable, architecture et construction (AC), systemes d'information et numerique (SIN), methodologie de projet et langues vivantes techniques. Tronc commun : arrete du 17 janvier 2019 (NOR MENE1901585A, langues vivantes) et programme d'enseignement moral et civique. Ressources : eduscol « Programmes et ressources en serie STI2D », « Developpement durable » et « Baccalaureat technologique STI2D » ; Agenda 2030 des Nations unies et objectifs de developpement durable.
points: A technical report communicates a method, results and a conclusion in a clear and verifiable way.
Its usual structure is : title, summary, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion and references.
The summary, or abstract, gives the objective, the main method and the key result in about 150 words.
The method section describes the equipment, the procedure and the conditions so that the experiment can be repeated.
The results section presents the measurements with tables, graphs and units, without interpretation.
The discussion explains the results, compares them with the requirements and discusses the uncertainties.
The conclusion answers the objective and proposes improvements or further work.
Technical writing uses the passive voice to describe procedures : the temperature was measured with a thermocouple.
The past simple is used for completed actions, the present simple for general conclusions.
Numbers and units follow international rules : a space between the value and the unit, a dot as decimal separator in English.
Figures and tables must have a number, a title and a reference in the text.
References cite the sources used : datasheets, standards, handbooks and previous reports.

questions.q: What is the role of an abstract ?
options: To summarise objective, method and key result
questions.correction: The abstract allows a reader to decide whether to read the full report.

questions.q: Which section describes the equipment and procedure ?
questions.correction: The method section must allow repetition of the experiment.

questions.q: Where should interpretation of results appear ?
questions.correction: Results present facts, discussion explains them.

questions.q: Which tense is used for a completed experiment ?
questions.correction: Completed actions are described with the past simple, often in the passive voice.

questions.q: How is a figure referenced in a report ?
options: By a number and a title mentioned in the text
questions.correction: Every figure must be cited in the text and have a caption.

questions.q: What should the conclusion contain ?
options: The answer to the objective and possible improvements
questions.correction: The conclusion closes the work and opens perspectives.

questions.q: Why cite datasheets and standards ?
options: To allow verification and credit sources
questions.correction: References ensure traceability and avoid plagiarism.

questions.q: Draft a short abstract for a report on the energy consumption of a solar charging station.
questions.reponse: A possible abstract is: 'This report presents the design and testing of a solar charging station for electric bicycles. The objective was to evaluate the daily energy produced and the charging time available on a school campus. A 100 W photovoltaic panel, a charge controller and a 12 V battery were installed and monitored for two weeks. Current and voltage were measured every minute and stored in a data logger. The results show an average production of 0,55 kWh per day, sufficient for two complete charges. The discussion analyses the influence of cloud cover and the limits of the battery capacity. The study concludes that the station is suitable for light use and proposes a larger panel for winter conditions.' This abstract states the objective, the method, a quantitative result and a conclusion in a compact form.
questions.correction: On attend objectif, methode, resultat chiffre et conclusion en environ 150 mots.

questions.q: Explain why the results section should not contain interpretation.
questions.reponse: The results section is a factual record : it presents measurements, tables and graphs so that the reader can check them. If the author mixes facts and interpretations, the reader cannot distinguish what was observed from what the author believes. For example, writing 'the efficiency was low because the sensor was badly placed' combines a measurement with a hypothesis. The measurement belongs to the results, the hypothesis to the discussion. Separating the two makes the report more rigorous and allows another reader to propose a different explanation from the same data. The discussion can then compare the results with the requirements, examine uncertainties and suggest causes, clearly identified as interpretations.
questions.correction: On separe faits mesures et hypotheses, avec un exemple et le benefit pour le lecteur.

Tronc commun : arrete du 17 janvier 2019 (NOR MENE1901585A, langues vivantes) et programme d'enseignement moral et civique. points: A job interview in English tests technical knowledge, communication and motivation.
The opening is short : greet the interviewer, thank him or her and give your name and role.
A self-introduction answers three questions : who you are, what you studied and what experience you have.
Technical vocabulary must be precise : prototype, assembly, tolerance, maintenance, commissioning, quality control.
The STAR method structures an answer to a behavioural question : Situation, Task, Action, Result.
A good answer gives a concrete example and a measurable result rather than a general claim.
Questions about a project should mention the constraint, the choice made and the reason for that choice.
When you do not understand a question, ask for clarification politely before answering.
The phrase 'Could you clarify what you mean by...' is useful and professional.
Avoid translating word for word from French : use simple and direct English sentences.
Preparing questions for the interviewer shows interest in the company and the role.
After the interview, a short thank-you message confirms your motivation and recalls one key point.

questions.q: What does the S in the STAR method mean ?
questions.correction: STAR stands for Situation, Task, Action, Result.

questions.q: Which answer is the strongest ?
options: I am very good at projects
In my last project I reduced the assembly time by 20 %
questions.correction: A concrete example with a measurable result is convincing.

questions.q: How to ask for clarification politely ?
options: Could you clarify what you mean by... ?
questions.correction: A polite reformulation shows active listening.

questions.q: Which word belongs to technical vocabulary ?
questions.correction: Commissioning is the phase of putting an installation into service.

questions.q: What should a self-introduction include ?
options: Who you are, your studies and your experience
questions.correction: The introduction gives a concise professional profile.

questions.q: Why prepare questions for the interviewer ?
options: To show interest in the role and the company
questions.correction: Relevant questions demonstrate motivation and reflection.

questions.q: What is a good post-interview action ?
options: Send a short thank-you message recalling a key point
questions.correction: A brief thank-you note confirms interest and leaves a clear memory.

questions.q: Prepare a one-minute self-introduction for a STI2D graduate applying for a technician position in automation.
questions.reponse: A possible introduction is: 'Good morning. My name is Alex Martin and I recently obtained a STI2D baccalaureate with a speciality in information systems and digital technology. During my final year, I worked in a team of four to design and test a prototype of a temperature monitoring station. I was responsible for the sensors and the data acquisition, and I learned to use a data logger and to compare measurements with the requirements. I also completed a two-month internship in a workshop, where I helped to maintain industrial controllers. I am interested in this position because I want to work on real automation systems and continue to learn from experienced technicians. Thank you.' This introduction is short, factual and directly connected to the job.
questions.correction: On attend nom, formation, projet concret, competence technique et motivation pour le poste.

questions.q: Using the STAR method, answer the question: 'Tell me about a time you solved a technical problem.'
questions.reponse: A possible answer is: 'Situation: during my final project, the temperature sensor gave unstable readings. Task: I had to find the cause before the final demonstration. Action: I checked the power supply and the wiring, then I compared the signal with a reference sensor and discovered that a poor connection introduced noise. I replaced the connector and added a filter in the acquisition software. Result: the readings became stable and the prototype passed the test. I also wrote the procedure in the project report so that the team could reuse it.' This answer gives a real situation, a precise action and a result that can be checked. It also shows documentation and teamwork, which are valued in a technical role.
questions.correction: On attend les quatre etapes STAR, une cause identifiee et un resultat concret.
